memory_update.text: LRN is the cleanest US-listed direct exposure to K-12 virtual schooling and career learning because its revenue is materially tied to virtual/blended public-school services and Career Learning.
PSO is the second cleanest large-cap direct exposure through Connections Academy/Pearson Virtual Schools and a growing CTE/career-readiness credential stack.
NRDY is a below-$1B exception because Varsity Tutors directly targets K-12 tutoring, district intervention, and AI-enhanced live instruction.

The likely chokepoint for this node is not curriculum alone; it is the combination of state/district authorization, recurring public funding, school operations, parent trust, teacher capacity, and demonstrable student outcomes.

Several strong node-relevant businesses appear private or nonprofit and are therefore not direct US-listed candidates in this pass: Imagine Learning/Edgenuity, Edmentum, HMH, Apex Learning, Renaissance, NWEA, Cambium, Amplify, Khan Academy, and many state-run virtual schools.

node: K-12 virtual schooling, tutoring, credit recovery, and career/technical pathways
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the K-12 virtual schooling, tutoring/intervention, digital curriculum, and career-pathway node. The most direct public exposures found are Stride and Pearson, both operating K-12 virtual school platforms with public-school or district relationships. Smaller-cap direct exposure exists through Nerdy/Varsity Tutors in online tutoring and intervention. Scholastic and Graham Holdings/Kaplan are included as adjacent public suppliers or platform owners tied to K-12 curriculum, school solutions, pre-college, and career exploration, but their chokepoint exposure is less pure than Stride/Pearson. Several highly relevant operators in credit recovery, virtual curriculum, and assessments appear private or nonprofit, creating a public-market coverage gap.
